newsitem.title: PERU: Force not answer to Peru siege - freed UK hostage.
newsitem.headline: Force not answer to Peru siege - freed UK hostage.

text.p: British diplomat Roger Church, released by Marxist rebels holding the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence in Peru, said on Monday the crisis could not be solved by force.
"I hope it will be resolved through negotiation. That is the only way out," Church told a news conference. "There is not going to be a violent solution to this at all."

Church, the deputy head of mission at the British embassy in Lima, was released in a group of 225 hostages on Sunday night. He said he believed there was "room for negotiation" to end the crisis, now in its sixth day.
"The Peruvian government wants to negotiate" a way out of the crisis, said Church, the only British diplomat to be taken hostage by the Tupac Amaru revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas.

British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkin said he was "delighted" that Church and David Griffith, a Lima hotel manager and the other Briton released on Sunday, "will be reunited with their families for Christmas."
Since about 20 rebels stormed the residence last Tuesday and threatened to kill all their hostages, they have released roughly 360 captives, but still hold about 140 high-profile hostages.
President Alberto Fujimori has refused to consider their main demand that jailed rebel comrades be released.
Church said he believed the original guerrilla demand that more than 400 comrades be freed had "been reduced somewhat" but he did not go into details.
The treatement of hostages inside the compound had been "as good as could be expected", he added.
"As far as I know there had been no mistreatment of hostages," Church said.
